chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ، الْحَضْرَمِيُّ، كُوفِيٌّ. ضَعِيفٌ - أَيْضًا - غَالٍ، مُتَهَافِتٌ، لَا ارْتِفَاعَ بِهِ.

translations.en: Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, al-Hadrami, Kufan. Weak – also – a ghālī (proponents of exaggeration), collapsed/unstable, there is no ascension (irtifāʿ) by him.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim al-Ḥaḍramī, a Kufan narrator, as not only weak (*daʿif*) but also a *ghālī* (exaggerator, often associated with the Ghulat sects) and *mutahafit* (unstable or collapsed in his memory). The term *mutahafit* specifically denotes a narrator whose hadiths have lost their structural integrity or reliability, rendering them unsuitable for establishing strong legal or theological proofs in Shia scholarship.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami in Shia hadith sciences?
